bio: K. M. Safin Kamal is a Lecturer in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at East West University. His research spans Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Medical Computer Vision (oncology, hematology, and radiography diagnostics), and Energy-Aware Distributed Systems. With 46 scholarly publications and 40 verified citations, his work advances automated healthcare intelligence and sustainable cloud computing.

researchPillars.title: Biomedical AI & Oncology
researchPillars.description: High-accuracy multi-class hematology classification (anemia, leukemia), MRI scan tumor detection, and explainable AI (Grad-CAM) for pneumonia in chest radiographs.

researchPillars.title: Edge Computer Vision & Remote Sensing
researchPillars.description: Automated digital license plate recognition, soil classification for smart agriculture, forest cover type voting classifiers, and multi-scale CNN transfer learning.

researchPillars.title: Green Cloud & Distributed Computing
researchPillars.description: Greedy algorithmic task scheduling, renewable energy load balancing, and carbon emission minimization for blockchain mining and modern datacenters.

researchPillars.title: Privacy, Federated AI & Security
researchPillars.description: Privacy-preserving federated ensemble learning for decentralized healthcare models, defensive spyware analysis, and secure multi-agent systems.

projects.title: OncoVision AI: Multi-Modal Deep Neural Ensemble for Clinical Oncology
projects.summary: Convolutional neural architecture and feature attribution pipeline analyzing peripheral blood smears and whole slide biopsy imaging for early-stage leukemia and carcinoma diagnosis.
highlights: Automated leukocyte morphology segmentation and blast cell classification
Grad-CAM visual attribution maps providing interpretable clinical evidence to hematologists
Extensively validated against EWU medical partner clinical benchmark datasets

projects.title: GreenCloud: Carbon-Aware Dynamic Task Orchestrator
projects.summary: Algorithmic distributed task scheduler that dynamically schedules cloud workloads across geo-distributed compute clusters powered by intermittent solar and wind grids.
highlights: Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) workload balancing
Greedy heuristics tailored for intermittent renewable energy profiles
Evaluated on real-world datacenter and distributed computing traces

projects.title: AgriSense: Remote Sensing & Soil Classification Neural Engine
projects.summary: Satellite and UAV drone aerial computer vision system classifying soil categories and land cover types for automated precision agriculture and forestry management.
highlights: Multi-spectral remote sensing band fusion and texture feature analysis
High-precision soil nutrient and terrain suitability prediction
Voting ensemble architectures surpassing baseline transfer learning

projects.title: AutoPlate-Edge: Low-Latency License Plate Neural Recognition
projects.summary: Embedded edge neural inference pipeline capable of real-time license plate detection and character recognition under varying weather, angle, and low-light conditions.
highlights: Night-time luminance correction using adaptive histogram equalization
Robust character segmentation resilient to Bengali and English fonts
Deployable on constrained edge devices (Raspberry Pi & Jetson Nano)

projects.title: HealthShield: Privacy-Preserving Federated Clinical Ensemble
projects.summary: Decentralized federated machine learning framework allowing hospitals and diagnostic labs to collaboratively train diagnostic models without transferring sensitive patient health data.
highlights: Byzantine-robust gradient aggregation resisting adversarial data poisoning
Strict HIPAA/GDPR clinical compliance through local compute boundaries
Minimal communication overhead through federated parameter quantization

teachingInfo.tagline: Lecturer at East West University, educating undergraduate engineers in deep learning, algorithms, pattern recognition, and supervising peer-reviewed capstone research.
teachingInfo.philosophyTitle: Teaching Philosophy: Rigorous Theory with Reproducible Empirical Code
teachingInfo.philosophyText: My teaching pedagogy bridges mathematical rigor with hands-on computational reproducibility. Whether deriving backpropagation gradients on the whiteboard or profiling PyTorch GPU tensors, students are trained not merely as tool consumers, but as rigorous researchers capable of questioning architectures, interpreting loss landscapes, and deploying models with ethical awareness.
